newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank chair sees support for EMU up after '99.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank chair sees support for EMU up after '99.

text.p: Sweden's central bank chairman, Kjell Olof Feldt, said on Tuesday Swedes' attitude towards Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) was likely to be more positive after 1999 even if Sweden stayed outside.
"An optimistic sign is that Sweden in this case will join at a later stage because wider popular support will develop for the union," Feldt told a seminar on EMU and Swedish business.
He said support for EMU would grow as there would be a lot of transactions carried out in the euro even if Sweden was not a member.
"Therefore it will seem unnatural if we don't join in the future," he said.
He said the ruling Social Democratic government's decision on EMU now would not hold forever.
The Social Democratic party leaders are due to make a decision on whether Sweden should join EMU this spring. It will be put to the party's congress in autumn.
"It is impossible for the parliament to make a decision that we never join the monetary union," Feldt said.
Feldt said a decision that Sweden is not yet ready for EMU would be much better.
"Then we are signalling that we are on the way and that is a huge difference," he said.
